answer: An agent economy can cap identities by auctioning a limited number of identity slots each period. Like quartz forming slowly under pressure, a valid identity takes time and a burned entry fee to mint, so spawning thousands becomes prohibitively expensive. Each slot sits at a vertex of the trust graph, and its holder must keep doing useful work; idle or abusive identities lose their slot at the next horizon, when slots are re-auctioned. Attackers therefore face a recurring, rising cost rather than a one-time trick, while honest agents keep cheap renewal through good conduct.
